The failing test `testOptionGroupLong` in `GnuParserTest` is trying to select an option with a long name within an `OptionGroup`. The bug report mentions that when the selected option doesn't have a short name, calling `group.setSelected(option)` has no effect.

By looking at the implementation of `OptionGroup.setSelected(Option)`, we can see that it sets the `selected` member variable based on the option's short name. If no option has been selected or the same option is being reselected, it sets the `selected` member variable to the option's short name. Otherwise, it throws an `AlreadySelectedException`.

The issue seems to be related to the fact that the `Option` being passed to `group.setSelected(option)` during the test run does not have a short name, leading to the `selected` member variable not being set as expected.

Additionally, I found that the `org.apache.commons.cli.OptionBuilder.create()` method throws an `IllegalArgumentException` if the `longopt` is null, indicating that the long name must be specified. This may be related to the issue in the test.

To resolve this bug, the test should use options with both a long and short name when adding them to the `OptionGroup`, ensuring that a valid `Option` object is passed to `group.setSelected(option)`.

Next, I will provide the methods that need to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
```java
org.apache.commons.cli.OptionGroup.setSelected(org.apache.commons.cli.Option)
org.apache.commons.cli.OptionBuilder.create()
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
